summary: George Peiris Malalasekera (1899–1973) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at SOAS and the University of London under Caroline A. F. Rhys Davids and William Stede. He taught at Ceylon University College (~1927–1942) and the University of Ceylon (~1942–1957).
George R. Elder worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman, attested in 1978.

George Roerich (1902–1960) worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of London, Harvard, and under Lobsang Mingyur Dorje. From ~1957 to 1960, he headed the philosophy department at the Institute of Oriental Studies.

George Santayana (1863–1952) was a philosopher. He studied at Harvard College, Humboldt University of Berlin, King's College, and Harvard University, completing his doctorate under William James (~1886–1889). He held a post at Harvard University from ~1889 to 1912.
George Sessions (1936–2016) was a scholar in philosophy who held posts at Sierra College in 1992–1993 and in 2002.
George Shirt (1843–1886) worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge by 1864 and studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington (~1864–1866).

George Thibaut (1848–1914) was an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber in 1867. He served as Direktor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1879–1888), Principal at Muir Central College (~1888–1906), and held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1906–1914).
George Watt (1851–1930) studied at the University of Glasgow and the University of Aberdeen. He held a post at the University of Calcutta from ~1873 to 1884.

George van Driem (born 1957) is a scholar of linguistics and Tibetology who earned his doctorate at Leiden University. He held posts at Leiden University (~1989–2009), the University of Bern (2010–2022), and the Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati (2020).

Georges Dreyfus (born 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics and earned his doctorate at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He has held a professorship at Williams College since ~1992.

Georges-Jean Pinault (born 1955) works in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at École Normale Supérieure (1974) and held posts at Blaise Pascal University (~1984–1995) and École Pratique des Hautes Études as professor (1999).

Georgios T. Halkias (born 1967) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble (~2001–2006) and held posts at the Warburg Institute, SOAS, Ruhr University Bochum, and the University of Hong Kong.

Gerald James Larson (1938–2019) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, studying at Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University. He was Professor of Religious Studies at UC Santa Barbara (~1970–1995) and Tagore Professor at Indiana University (~1995–2003).

Gereon Kopf (born 1965) specializes in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Temple University (~1992–1996) and under Yasuo Yuasa. He held positions at J. F. Oberlin, Nanzan Institute, Luther College (~1997), and the University of Hong Kong.

Gergely Hidas works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford (Balliol College) under Alexis Sanderson (2002–2008), and held posts at Eötvös Loránd University (2007–2014) and the British Museum (2014).

Gerhard Oberhammer (1929–2025) was an Indologist and philosopher. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Innsbruck (~1947–1954) and studied under Erich Frauwallner and V. Raghavan. He held posts at Utrecht University (1961) and the University of Vienna (1964).

Geshe Gendun Lodro (1924–1979) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Drepung Monastery (~1947–1961) under Khensur Ngawang Lekden. He served on the faculty at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, the University of Hamburg (1967), and the University of Virginia (~1979).
Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Gyume Tantric College (attested 1987) and Sera Monastery (attested 1992).

Geshe Lhundub Sopa (1923–2014) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ganden Chokhor and Sera Jey Monastery. He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1967 through the 1990s as a professor of Buddhist and South Asian studies.
Geshe Lobsang Tenzin worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held a post at Sera Monastery (attested 1980) and served as abbot at Gyume Tantric College (attested 1987).
